# Normal distribution

$$X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)$$

Parameters: $\mu$ and $\sigma$.

The center of every normal distribution is controlled by it's expected value or $\mu$.The height of the normal distribution is controlled by it's standard deviation, $\sigma$. The higher the curve, lower is the deviation.

# R functions for the normal distribution

d,p,q functions: dnorm, pnorm and qnorm. By default, dnorm(x, mean, sd), mean = 0 and sd = 1

Example: N(20, 0.5)

```{r}
gnorm(20, 0.5)
```


- `dnorm(x)`: density of a point x (height of the density curve)

```{r}
dnorm(19, 20, 0.5)

dnorm(10, 20, 0.5) # since this cont rv the probability further from the curve is almost zero.

tibble(`f(x)` = dnorm(seq(19, 20, by = 0.001), 20, 0.5))
```

- `pnorm(q)`: prob/area to the left of a point q (by default), if using `lower.tail = F` this would instead give you the prob/area to the right.

```{r}
pnorm(19, 20, 0.5) # P(X <= 19) = P(X < 19) 

sum(dnorm(0:19, 20, 0.5)) #this is not the same as the prob to the left, because dnorm doesn't give prob

pnorm(19, 20, 0.5)
pnorm(19.000001, 20, 0.5)

pnorm(19, 20, 0.5, lower.tail = F) # P(X > 19) = P(X >= 19)
1 - pnorm(19, 20, 0.5)
```

- `qnorm(p)`: give us a point that covers a certain prob to the left of it (by default)


```{r}
qnorm(0.9, 20, 0.5)
qnorm(0.9001, 20, 0.5)

qnorm(0.9, 20, 0.5)
qnorm(0.9, 20, 0.5, lower.tail = F)

20.64078 - 20
19.35922 - 20

gnorm(0, 0.5) + 
  geom_norm_fill(0, 0.5, b = qnorm(0.9, 0, 0.5), fill = "yellow", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_norm_fill(0, 0.5, a = qnorm(0.9, 0, 0.5, lower.tail = F), fill = "purple", alpha = 0.5) 

```


# Demonstration of CLT

In this example, we start with a random variable X which is Uniformly distributed, i.e,

$$X \sim Unif(2,5)$$

So the $\mu= \frac{(a+b)}{2}=3.5$ and $\sigma = \frac{b-a}{\sqrt{12}} = 2.02$. 

Due to CLT, we know that the sample of size 100 from X will have a normal distribution, i.e,

$$\overline{X} \sim N(\mu, \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}})$$

```{r}
xbar = c()
for (i in 1:1000) {
  x_i = runif(100, 2, 5) #sample of X of size 100. X has a expected value of (a+b)/2 which (2+5)/2
xbar[i] = mean(x_i) # sample mean/avg of X
}

sd(xbar) # this number gives the deviation of the xbars and should approx be the same as sigma/sqrt(n) = 2.02/10. Any differences you see here is due to this being sample deviation and not the population deviation.



library(tidyverse)
ggplot(mapping = aes(xbar)) + geom_density() + geom_vline(xintercept = (2+5)/2, col = "red")
```


In this example, we start with a random variable X which is exponentially distributed, i.e,

$$X \sim exp(0.1)$$

```{r}
xbar = c()
for (i in 1:1000) {
  x_i = rexp(1000, 0.1) # here since X is from a skewed distribution only a bigger sample size gives a normal distribution
xbar[i] = mean(x_i)
}

xbar

ggplot(mapping = aes(xbar)) + geom_density() + geom_vline(xintercept = 1/0.1, # the expected value of X is 1/lambda = 1/0.1
           col = "red")
```
